questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: On a compressed gas tank, liquid discharge valves must be open during loading and unloading. They should be closed at all other times.

questions.question: The only effective way to check tire pressure is:

options.text: By pushing on the tire to feel the pressure.

questions.explanation: Check your tires before each trip. Use a tire pressure gauge to check tire pressure. This is the only accurate method.

questions.question: Who must mark and label materials for shipping?
questions.explanation: Shippers must warn drivers and others about hazardous materials. They do this by labeling packages, placing placards on vehicles, and providing shipping papers and emergency information.

questions.question: At an accident scene, which task is NOT your job as a driver?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to put out a hazardous materials fire yourself.
Telling emergency responders about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to put out a hazardous materials fire yourself.
questions.explanation: Your job is to keep people away, limit material spread if safe, tell emergency personnel about the hazards, and provide shipping papers. Do not fight hazardous materials fires unless you have special training and equipment.

questions.question: What does a shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers must include details about the specific hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: A material's hazard class shows:

options.text: The risks associated with the material.
How quickly the material must reach its destination.

questions.correctAnswerText: The risks associated with the material.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are divided into nine classes. Each class explains the type of risks the material poses.

questions.question: A placarded vehicle's power unit must carry a fire extinguisher rated at least:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's power unit must have a fire extinguisher rated 10 B:C or higher by Underwriters Laboratories (UL).

questions.question: Shippers package hazardous materials to ____ them.
questions.explanation: Shippers package hazardous materials to keep them fully contained. Vehicles must have placards to show what cargo they carry.

questions.question: ____ warn others about hazardous materials.
questions.explanation: Placards are diamond-shaped signs placed on packages and vehicles to warn others about hazardous materials. Shippers place them. Drivers must check that the correct placards are used.

questions.question: When loading hazardous materials containers, do not use:
questions.explanation: Protect containers of hazardous materials. Do not use equipment that could damage containers, such as hooks.

questions.question: Which agency performs the background check for a new or renewed HazMat endorsement?
questions.explanation: The Transportation Security Administration (TSA) conducts the federal security check for HazMat endorsements.

questions.question: What must be in the vehicle when transporting chlorine?
questions.explanation: Drivers must have an approved gas mask in their vehicle when transporting chlorine in cargo tanks.

questions.question: What should you do if a hazardous materials label will not fit on the package?

options.text: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
Attach a QR Code to be scanned.
Reduce the size of the HazMat label to fit it on the item.

questions.correctAnswerText: Place the label on a tag securely attached to the item.
questions.explanation: If a label does not fit on the package, attach it to a tag that is securely fastened to the package.

questions.question: When loading corrosive materials, what should you NOT do?
questions.explanation: Keep corrosive containers upright. Do not drop or roll them when loading.

questions.question: Where can you find identification numbers for chemicals?

options.text: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
In the Periodic Table of Elements.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the DOT Emergency Response Guide.
questions.explanation: The Department of Transportation (DOT) Emergency Response Guide lists chemical identification numbers and is organized by substance names and ID numbers.

questions.question: When refueling a vehicle carrying hazardous materials, what should you do?

options.text: The engine should be left on.
The engine should be turned off.
The gas nozzle may be left unattended.

questions.correctAnswerText: The engine should be turned off.
questions.explanation: Turn off the engine before refueling. Someone must always be at the nozzle to control the fuel flow.

questions.question: What is important to know about transporting radioactive materials?

options.text: Radiation spreads from the package and passes through to other packages.
The package should be transported in the cab.
The package should be loaded on its side.

questions.correctAnswerText: Radiation spreads from the package and passes through to other packages.
questions.explanation: Radiation spreads from radioactive packages and can reach nearby packages. Rules limit how many packages can be loaded together.

questions.question: When carrying Division 1.1 explosives, how far must you park from any building?
questions.explanation: When carrying Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 explosives, park at least 300 feet away from buildings, bridges, tunnels, gathering places, or open fires.

questions.question: Where should a hazardous material's identification number appear?

options.text: On a sticker near the shipping container.

questions.explanation: The ID number must appear on the packaging, shipping papers, cargo tanks, and other bulk containers.

questions.question: What must a box display if it contains liquid containers?

options.text: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
The number of containers inside the box.

questions.correctAnswerText: Arrows pointing in the correct upright direction.
questions.explanation: Boxes with liquid containers must have arrows showing the correct upright direction.

questions.question: Besides reading the manual, what is the best way to learn about transporting hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The manual has all the information you need to pass the test. However, you should also attend hazardous materials training courses. You can also learn more by reading federal and state rules about transporting hazardous materials.

questions.question: Why might opening trailer doors during a cargo fire cause the fire to spread?

options.text: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
It changes the temperature inside the trailer.
It adds moisture to the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows oxygen into the trailer.
questions.explanation: Do not open trailer doors during a cargo fire. Opening them lets oxygen inside, which can cause the fire to grow and spread.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo catches fire, what should you do?

options.text: Try to put it out with a fire extinguisher.
Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
Wait for the fire to go out on its own.

questions.correctAnswerText: Call emergency personnel and let them fight the fire.
questions.explanation: Fighting a hazardous materials fire requires special training and protective gear. Do not try to fight the fire yourself unless you have the proper equipment and training.

questions.question: If hazardous materials cargo is leaking and the driver has no phone, what should they do?

options.text: Drive to find a phone to call emergency personnel.
Drive to a hazardous materials clean-up facility.
Send someone else to get help.

questions.correctAnswerText: Send someone else to get help.
questions.explanation: If hazardous materials are leaking, do not drive. Driving spreads contamination over a larger area. Park your vehicle safely, stay with it, and have someone else get help. Do not leave the vehicle.

questions.question: When transporting Division 1.3 materials, the floor liner must be made from:
questions.explanation: When transporting Division 1.1, 1.2, or 1.3 materials, use a floor liner. The liner must be tight and made from non-metallic material or non-ferrous metal. Non-ferrous metals do not contain iron.

questions.question: What should a driver check to verify hazardous materials are correct?

options.text: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
The shipping paper is written in code.
All packages are labeled as poison.

questions.correctAnswerText: The shipping paper matches the markings and labels on packages.
questions.explanation: Compare the package markings and labels to the shipping papers. Make sure the shipper listed the correct basic description on the shipping paper and put the correct labels on the packages.

questions.question: Before opening trailer doors during a minor truck fire, what should you do?

options.text: Check if the doors are hot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check if the doors are hot.
questions.explanation: Before opening trailer doors during a truck fire, touch the doors to see if they are hot. If the doors are hot, there may be a fire inside the cargo. Keep the doors closed if you suspect a cargo fire.

questions.question: How many identical placards must be on a vehicle?
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle must have four identical placards. Place one on the front, one on the back, and one on each side.

questions.question: What must you do when approaching a railroad crossing while carrying chlorine?

options.text: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
You must slow down before crossing the tracks.
You can cross if no warning lights are flashing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop before crossing the tracks.
questions.explanation: If transporting any amount of chlorine, always stop at a railroad crossing. Stop 15 to 50 feet from the nearest track, even if you do not see a train.

questions.question: If cargo is leaking, how should you identify the hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: If cargo is leaking, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not touch or smell the leaking materials. This could cause injury or death.
